la:verb:offendo.gloss: to hit, thrust, strike against something
senses: to hit, thrust, strike against something
to suffer damage, receive an injury
to stumble, blunder, commit offence or sin
to shock, vex, offend, mortify, scandalize
la:verb:offendo.html:
offendo, di, sum, 3, v. a. and n.
obfendo
.
to hit, thrust, strike, or dash against something (syn.: illido, impingo; class.).
Lit.: offendere caput ad fornicem,: latus vehementer,: coxam,to hurt himself in the haunch,: pedem, Auct. B. Hisp. 23; : solido,against something solid,: in scopulis offendit puppis,strikes on,: in redeundo offenderunt,ran aground,: in cornua,: ne quem in cursu capite, aut cubito, aut pectore offendam, aut genu,: visco,.—
Transf., to hit upon, light upon a person or thing, i. e. to come upon, meet with, find (syn.: deprehendo, invenio): si te hic offendero, moriere, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 301 Vahl.); cf. : haec, cum ego a foro revortar, facite ut offendam parata,: paululum si cessassem, Domi non offendissem,: si te in plateā offendero hac post umquam, periisti,; : imparatum te offendam,will come upon you unawares, will surprise you,: eundem bonorum sensum,: nondum perfectum templum offendere,: omnia aliter ac jusserat offendit,.—
Trop.
In gen., to suffer damage, receive an injury: quis est tam Lynceus, qui in tantis tenebris nihil offendat, nusquam incurrat?: in causis,: ad fortunam,.—
In partic., to stumble, blunder, make a mistake, commit a fault; to commit an offence, to be offensive (syn.: pecco, delinquo): in quo ipsi offendissent, alios reprehendissent,: sin quid offenderit, sibi totum, tibi nihil offenderit,: offendebant illi quidem apud gravīs et honestos homines, sed populi judiciis florebant,gave offence to,: se apud plebem offendisse de aerario,: neque in eo solum offenderat, quod,: legi, to offend against or violate the law, .—Hence (eccl. Lat.), to offend, commit a sin: in multis enim offendimus omnes,.— Of things, to be offensive: cum nihil aliud offenderit,; cf. .—
To find fault with, be displeased with, take offence at any thing: at credo, in Caesarem probatis, in me offenditis,: si in me aliquid offendistis,have taken any offence at me,.—
To fail in any thing, i. e. to have a misfortune, to be unfortunate, meet with ill success: apud judices offendere, opp. causam iis probare,: cum multi viri fortes offenderint,: tamquam M. Atilius primo accessu ad Africam offenderit,i. e. met with a calamity,; cf. I. A. supra.—Impers. pass.: sin aliquid esset offensum,: quoties culpā ducis esset offensum,might have met with a defeat,; cf.: nullum ejusmodi casum exspectans, quo . . . in milibus passuum tribus offendi posset, Kraner ad loc.: at si valetudo ejus offendissit,failed,.—
To shock, offend, mortify, vex, displease one: me exquisisse aliquid, in quo te offenderem,: tuam existimationem,: neminem umquam non re, non verbo, non vultu denique offendit,: offensus nemo contumeliā,: ne offendam patrem,: ut eos splendor offendat,: extinctum lumen recens offendit nares,: offendere tot caligas, tot Milia clavorum,provoke,: polypodion offendit stomachum,disagrees with,: ne colorum claritas aciem oculorum offenderet,.—Pass., to be displeased, feel hurt: multis rebus meus offendebatur animus,.— With inf.: ut non offendar subripi (ista munera),so that I am not offended at their being taken from me,: componi aliquid de se, offendebatur, he took it ill, if, etc., —Hence, of-fensus, a, um, P. a.
Offensive, odious (cf.: invisus, odiosus, infensus): miserum atque invidiosum offensumque ordinem senatorium!: offensum et invisum esse alicui,.—As subst.: offensum, i, n., the offence: offensum est quod eorum, qui audiunt, voluntatem laedit,.—
Offended, displeased, vexed, incensed, imbittered: offensus et alienatus animus,: aliena et offensa populi voluntas,: offensos merere

deos, : offensi animi regum, Auct. B. Alex. 32.—Comp.: quem cum esse offensiorem arbitrarer,: quem sibi offensiorem sciebat esse,; .
la:verb:offendo.inflection: di, sum, 3, v. a. and n.

la:noun:offensus.html:
offensus, ūs, m.
1. offendo
,
a striking against, a shock (poet. and in post-class. prose).
Lit., ; ; .—
Transf.
A lighting upon, meeting with: per offensus armorum,.—
An offence, vexation, annoyance: sin vita in offensu est,.

la:verb:offero.gloss: to bring before or bring to, present, offer, bestow, show, place before, exhibit, expose
senses: to bring before or bring to, present, offer, bestow, show, place before, exhibit, expose
to offer to God, consecrate, dedicate
la:verb:offero.html:
offĕro (obf-), obtŭli, oblātum, v. a.
ob-fero
,
to bring before; to present, offer; to show, exhibit (class.; cf. obicio, ostendo).
In gen.: incommode illis fors obtulerat adventum meum,; cf.: opportune te obtulisti mihi obviam,; ; : strictamque aciem venientibus offert,presents, opposes,: speciem offerre,to present a false appearance,.—In pass.: offerri, mid., to show one's self, appear; to meet, encounter: multis in difficillimis rebus praesens auxilium ejus (numinis) oblatum est,: oblata religio est,a religious scruple struck him,: metu oblato,: lex quaedam videbatur oblata,.—
In partic.
To offer, expose; to bring forward, adduce: ne offeramus nos periculis sine causā,; so, se morti,: se ad mortem,: obtulimus nos ad prima pericula,: vitam in discrimen,: moram offerre alicui,: nam tu nunc vides pro tuo caro capite carum offerre me meum caput vilitati,: sponte suā leto caput obvius optulit ipse,; cf. ; ; ; : criminibus oblatis,brought forward, adduced,.—
To offer, proffer; to bring, cause, occasion, confer, bestow; to inflict, etc. (cf. promitto, recipio, infero): foedus,: in omnia ultro suam offerens operam,: di tibi semper omnia optata offerant,: alicui optatissimum beneficium,: hoc tantum boni, quod vobis ab dis immortalibus oblatum et datum est,: datum atque oblatum,; : ut nunc hac re mihi opem et auxilium offeras, bring me aid and assistance, help me, Lucil. ap. : laetitiam,to procure,: alicui injuriam,: vitium virgini,: stuprum alicui,: mortem alicui,: sibi molestiam atque aerumnam offerre, to bring, procure, occasion, Lucil. ap. : occasio ad occupandam Asiam oblata, : seque offert suscepturum,offers,: rusticus offerebat se intercessurum senatus consulto,: oblatā facultate in castra sese receperunt,.—
In eccl. Lat.
To offer to God, to consecrate, dedicate, ; ; .—
To offer up, sacrifice, : Domino,: pro filio,: ex scelere,: semet ipsum Deo, et saep.

senses: obligation, an obligatory service, visit, or gesture
la:noun:officium.html:
offĭcĭum, ii, n.
for opificium, opus and facio
, qs. that which one does for another,
a service, whether of free will or of (external or moral) necessity (class.; cf.: studium, beneficium, meritum, munus).
A voluntary service, a kindness, favor, courtesy, rendered to one whose claim to it is recognized; while beneficium is a service rendered where there is no claim: officium esse filii, uxoris, earum personarum, quas necessitudo suscitat et ferre opem jubet,.
In gen.: altera sententia est, quae definit amicitiam paribus officiis ac voluntatibus,: odiosum sane genus hominum officia exprobrantium,: nihil est vicissitudine studiorum officiorumque jucundius,: filicem cum officio vicini decidere, so as to do him a service, Col. 2, 14, 6: summo officio praeditus homo,exceedingly obliging,. —
In partic.
A ceremonial observance, ceremony, attendance (on a festive or solemn occasion; mostly post-Aug.): officio togae virilis interfui,: sine solenni officio,: per sollenne nuptiarum celeberrimo officio deductum ad se,; cf. : ad officium venire,: relicto statim novorum consulum officio,: in officio salutationis,: vitans praeter navigantium officia,: officia prosequentium,: quod supremis in matrem officiis defuisset,at the payment of the last offices, at the funeral,: officium cras Primo sole mihi peragendum in valle Quirini,a ceremonial visit,; .—
In mal. part., compliance, favor, ; ; ; cf. virile,: puerile,; .—
In gen., an obligatory service, an obligation, duty, function, part, office (so most freq. in prose and poetry of all periods): nulla vitae pars neque publicis neque privatis neque forensibus neque domesticis in rebus, neque si tecum agas quid, neque, si cum altero contrahas, vacare oflicio potest: in eoque et colendo sita vitae est honestas omnis et in neglegendo turpitudo, etc.,: perfectum officium rectum opinor vocemus, quod Graeci κατόρθωμα: hoc autem commune καθῆκον vocant, ; an id doles, quia illi suum officium non colunt, quom tu tuum facis?; ; : meminisse officium suum,to remember one's duty,.—Also, subject., a sense of duty: si quis aegre ferat nihil in se esse virtutis, nihil officii, etc.,: quicquid in eum judicii officiique contuleris,: intellegere, utrum apud eos pudor atque officium an timor valeret,: suum facere,to do one's duty,: omnibus officiis amicitiae servatis,observe all the obligations of friendship,: exsequi,: fungi officio,: satisfacere officio,to perform,: officium suum deserere,to disregard one's duty, not perform it,: discedere ab officio,: deesse officio suo,: officii duxit,considered it his duty,.—Of animals: canes funguntur officiis luporum,act the part of,.—Of things: neque pes neque mens satis suum officium facit,: officium corporis, the function or property of a body, and 362.—
In partic.
Lit., an official duty, a service, employment, business (class.): toti officio maritimo M. Bibulus praepositus cuncta administrabat,naval service,; : celeriter equitatus ad cotidianum itineris officium revertitur,: confecto legationis officio,: destringor officio,: officium (scribae),.—
Transf., an office, appointment (post-Aug.).
Laboriosissimum et maximum, office, : nova officia excogitavit,; cf.: novum officium instituit a voluptatibus,: obligationes, quae non propriis viribus consistunt, neque officio judicis, neque praetoris imperio neque legis potestate confirmantur,: qui ex officio pro aliis interveniunt,by virtue of their office,: ministerii,: sacerdotum,.—
Transf., in concr.
The officials or attendants on a magistrate = officialium corpus (post-class.): sub praetextu adventus officiorum vel militum,; : deponere aliquid apud officium, officia palatina, officers at the imperial court, Treb. Poll. Gall. 17, 8.—
An office or court of a magistrate: ipse me Regulus convenit in praetoris officio,.

senses: to stand in the way of, oppose
to be detrimental or hurtful to
la:verb:officio.html:
offĭcĭo (obf-), ēci, ectum, 3, v. n. and a.
[ob-facio], to come in the way of, to hinder, oppose, thwart, obstruct (class.; syn. obsto).
Lit.
Neutr.: nunc quidem paululum, inquit, a sole: offecerat videlicet apricanti,hindered him from sunning himself, stood before him so as to intercept the sunshine,: luminibus, to obstruct one's light: jus vel altius tollendi aedes aut non tollendi, ne luminibus vicini officiatur,; ; ; ; 39, 1, 5 et saep.—So, in a fig.: nec mentis quasi luminibus officit altitudo fortunae et gloriae,: demoliri ea, quorum altitudo officeret auspiciis,: ipsa umbra terrae soli officiens noctem efficit,intervening before,: cum alii in angustiis ipsi sibi properantes officerent,: hostium itineri,: prospectui, Auct. B. Afr. 52.—
Act. (only ante- and post-class.): quapropter simul inter se retrahuntur et extra Officiuntur,are impeded,; ; (iter, Auct. B. Afr. 61, is prob. a gloss).—
Trop., to stand in the way of, to oppose, obstruct, to be detrimental or hurtful to, to hurt (cf.: obsisto, adversor, noceo): promitto tibi non offerturum,: cur te mihi offers, ac meis commodis, officio simulato, officis et obstas?; cf. : consiliis alicujus,: timor animi auribus officit,: nomini, i. e. famae, Liv. praef. 1: officiunt laetis frugibus herbae,hurt by shutting off light and moisture,: lactucae officiunt claritati oculorum,.—With quominus: nec vero Isocrati, quominus haberetur summus orator, offecit, quod, etc.,.
la:verb:officio.inflection: ēci, ectum, 3, v. n. and a.

offex, ĭcis, m.
officio
,

la:noun:offensio.html:
offensĭo, ōnis, f.
1. offendo
,
a striking against any thing; a tripping, stumbling (class.).
Lit.: pedis offensio,; in plur.: offensiones pedum,: dentium, Lact. Opif. Dei, 10, 13. —Absol.: offensione sonitūs,.—
Transf., that against which one stumbles, a stumbling-block: ut nihil offensionis haberet,.—
Trop.
An offence given to any one; hence,disfavor, aversion, disgust, dislike, hatred, discredit, bad reputation,; (for which: existimatio offensa nostri ordinis,, § 117): sapiens praetor offensionem vitat aequalitate decernendi,: suscipere invidiam atque offensionem apud aliquem,: in odium offensionemque populi Romani inruere,: cadere,: offensionem excipere,: subire,: adferre,: offensiones accendere,: hoc apud alios offensionem habet,displeases them,. —
An offence which one receives; displeasure, vexation: habere ad res certas vitiosam offensionem atque fastidium,: mihi majori offensioni sunt quam delectationi possessiunculae meae, give me more vexation than pleasure, .—
A complaint, indisposition; an accident, misfortune, mishap, failure: corporum offensiones,: graves solent offensiones esse ex gravibus morbis, si qua culpa commissa est,: habet enim nihil quod in offensione deperdat,i.e. if he loses his cause,: offensiones belli,misfortunes, defeats,: offensionum et repulsarum ignominia,i.e. refusals,.—
That which causes one to offend or sin, a stumbling-block (eccl. Lat.): unusquisque offensiones oculorum suorum abiciat,: nemini dantes ullam offensionem,: lapis offensionis, Pet. 2, 8 al.

la:adj:officiosus.html:
offĭcĭōsus, a, um, adj.
officium
.
Full of courtcousness or complaisance, obliging, ready to serve (esp. towards one's superiors; class.; syn. studiosus): homo,: amicitia,: sedulitas,: voluntas,.—Comp.: estne quisquam, qui tibi officiosior, liberaliorque videatur?; .—Sup.: officiosissima natio candidatorum,; for which with summe: homines Lampsaceni summe in omnes cives Romanos officiosi,.—
Dutiful, in accordance with duty: dolor,: labores,: pietas,.—
Subst.: offĭcĭō-sus, i, m., an official or attendant at a bath, .—Hence, adv.: offĭcĭōsē, courteously, obligingly (class.): officiose et amice factum,: aliquid facere, Afran. ap. P.: scribere,.—Comp.: gratum etiam Pilia (fecit), sed illa officiosius, quod, etc.,.—Sup.: officiosissime venit ad me, (32) init.

la:noun:offa.html:
offa, ae, f.
Lit., a bite, bit, morsel; esp. a little ball or pellet made of flour: antiqui offam vocabant abscisum globi formā, ut manu glomeratam pultem, Paul. ex Fest. s. v. poenitam offam, p. 242 Müll.: offam eripere alicui, Enn. ap. ( Vahl.); : offam obicit,: pultis,.—Prov.: inter os et offam, = Engl. between the cup and the lip, Cato ap. (17), 1; cf.: vetus est proverbium inter os et offam, idem significans quod Graecus ille παροιμιώδης versus: Πολλὰ μεταξὺ πέλει κύλικος και χείλεος ἄκρου, Apollin. ap. Gell. l. l. § 3.—
Transf., in gen.
A piece, lump, mass: aufer illam offam porcinam, Ritschl N. cr.: offa porcina cum caudā in cenis puris offa penita vocatur, Paul. ex Fest. s. v. penem, p. 230 Müll.: gummi in offas convolutum,.—
A swelling, .—
A shapeless mass, untimely birth, abortion, : quantas robusti carminis offas Ingeris?; .

offulgĕo (obf-), si, 2, v. n.
ob-fulgeo

Lit.: continuo nova lux oculis offulsit,: dextrum offulsit conatibus omen,: species mei amici, Ps. -.—
Trop.: lucrum, Ps. -: ortus imperii nostri,.

offulcĭo (obf-) (si), tum, 4, v. a.

offensĭo, ōnis, f.
1. offendo
,
a striking against any thing; a tripping, stumbling (class.).

la:noun:offensa.html:
offensa, ae, f.
1. offendo, like repulsa, from repello
,
a striking or grating against any thing.
Lit. (very rare): donec cerussae similis fiat, nulla dentium offensa,and does not grit against the teeth,: sine offensis fricantium,.—
Trop.
Offence, disfavor, displeasure, hatred; enmity: quin magnā in offensā sim apud Pompeium,, a, 2: quod offensae fuerit in istā cunctatione, te subisse, to incur hatred, Cael. ap. : gravissimam contrahere,to fall into disgrace,: offensam meruisse,: habere,to cause hatred,: ne minus gratiae quam offensae mereamur,: sinceri et sine offensā in diem Christi,.—
An offending against or violating a law, an offence, crime (mostly in jurid. Lat.): offensa edicti,: levis offensae contrahere culpam, Cod. Th. 4, 11, 1: sub quālibet culpae aut erroris offensā,: offensae veteris reus atque tacendae,.—
An injury received, an offence, affront, wrong (perh. only since the Aug. per.): gustus,: offensas vindicet ense suas,: in offensis exorabilis,: per ejusmodi offensas emetiendum est confragosum hoc iter,.—
Of a state of injury, a complaint, inconvenience, indisposition: sine offensā corporis animique,: si quid offensae in cenā sensit,indisposition,; ; cf. in plur., .

la:verb:offenso.html:
offenso, āvi, ātum, 1, v. freq. a.
1. offendo
,

Lit.: sponte suā offensando ut semina rerum,; so : omnes offensare capita,dash their heads against the wall,.—
Trop., to stumble, trip, falter in speaking, .—(Offensatus, , is a false reading for offensator, q.v.).

la:verb:offusco.html:

ob-fusco

la:verb:offundo.gloss: to pour or spread over, out, down etc.
senses: to pour or spread over, out, down etc.
la:verb:offundo.html:
offundo (obf-), ūdi, ūsum, 3, v. a.
obundo
.

To pour before or around; to pour out, pour down (class.).
Lit.: cibum (avibus),; .—
Transf., mid., to pour itself out; to spread, extend: ut piscibus aqua, nobis aër crassus offunditur,i. e. surrounds us,: rubor gravissimis quoque viris offunditur,: cum ignis oculorum cum eo igne, qui est ob os offusus, se confudit,: asinus offunditur,tumbles down,. —
Trop., to pour or spread out any thing over a person or thing: quasi noctem quandam rebus offundere,: haec indoctorum animis offusa caligo est,: tamquam si offusa rei publicae sempiterna nox esset,: omnium rerum terrorem oculis et auribus,: caliginem oculis,: pavorem incompositis,: errorem alicui,to cause,: quibus tenebris est offusa hominis cogitatio, Lact. de Ira, 1, 5; . 24, 7.—
To spread over, i. e. to cover a thing with something.
Lit.: ut obscuratur et offunditur luce solis lumen lucernae,eclipsed,: oculi clarissimā in luce tenebris offusi,.—
Trop.: offusus pavore,overcome,: Marcellorum meum pectus memoria obfudit,has filled, dub.: non existimare se tantis tenebris offusam esse rem pnblicam,; .

la:noun:officina.html:
offĭcīna, ae, f.
contr. from opificina, from opifex; the uncontracted prim. form, opĭfĭcīna, is still found in , and Mai
,
a workshop, manufactory (class.; cf. fabrica).
Lit.: nec enim quicquam ingenuum potest habere officina,: instituit officinam Syracusis in regiā maximam,: armorum,a manufactory of arms,; ; ; for which, ferraria, Auct. B. Afr. 20: aerariorum,: fullonum,: pictoris,: plastarum,: tingentium,: tonstrinarum,: promercalium vestium,a shop in which garments are made for sale,: cetariorum,a place where fish are salted,: officina monetae,: dum graves Cyclopum Volcanus ardens urit officinas,.—
In partic., in econom. lang. = ornithon, a place where fowls are kept, in order to lay their eggs and hatch their young, a poultry-house or yard, .—
Transf., a making, formation: in magnis corporibus facilis officina sequaci materia fuit,.—
Trop., a workshop, manufactory, laboratory: mathematici, poëtae, musici, medici denique ex hac tamquam omnium artium officinā profecti sunt,: falsorum commentariorum, et chirographorum officina,: nequitiae,: dicendi,: sapientiae,: spirandi pulmo,: rhetoris,: ex rhetorum officinis,: domus ejus officina eloquentiae habita est,: corruptelarum omnis generis,; cf. 39, 8, 7: crudelitatis,: humanarum calamitatium,.
